context:
Goal: filing your rulings never waits on a reviewer for no gain, and a new ruling never silently contradicts an old one.
Problem (risk): "skip review" means no reviewer agent reads the record before it merges; only the automatic checks run. Today no check compares a newly filed ruling against older rulings, so a ruling given in haste that contradicts one from months ago would merge with no flag to you.
Based on (ruling): docs-only-prs-skip-review (owner, 2026-09-26): a PR that changes only prose or docs, and touches no rule, guard, check or product code, gets no reviewer pass.
Based on (read): the past-ruling check already flags a new question that repeats or contradicts a past ruling, but it reads questions and reports, not records.
Based on (incident): degen PRs 370 and 378 waited on a reviewer for ruling records (degen page item 83).
Departs from: docs-only-prs-skip-review, unclear on ruling records — c skips the reviewer and adds a contradiction check on each ruling record.

options.gain: Records merge fast, and no new ruling quietly overrides an old one.
options.how: A ruling record merges on green checks. A check flags any new ruling record whose question already has a record (rule one record per question), so you see the old ruling before the new one lands.
options.label: Skip the reviewer, flag a clash
options.lose: One more check to build; it finds a clash by question, so a clash filed under a different question still needs your eye.

options.gain: A reader checks every filed ruling.
options.how: Each ruling record gets a short read against your quote and the older records.
options.label: A short reviewer read of each record
options.lose: Each ruling record waits on one more read, as degen's did.

options.how: A ruling record counts as docs only when it changes no rule text, guard, check or code; no new check.
options.label: As today
options.lose: A ruling that contradicts an old one merges with no flag.

reply: Landed: claude-settings #1232 merged in batch 10 (main 59bff081, Nov 5 06:36 CST); a ruling record gets one short reviewer read.
title: A record that files your ruling: skip the reviewer, but have a check flag it when it contradicts an older ruling?
why: Recommended: c. Your worry is a hasty ruling quietly overriding an old one; a contradiction check catches that without making every record wait for a reviewer.
